clue.text: Almost entirely indifferent about hot drink

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the abbreviation that follows
almost means not quite all, so the following word loses its final letter

parts.note: entirely means all of it
cool means unenthusiastic or indifferent
H is the standard abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone almost completely unmoved by a hot drink set in front of them.
explanation.walkthrough: Hot drink suggests tea or coffee, but the definition is just the last word and hot is only its usual one-letter abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcohol is the intoxicating ingredient of beer, wine and spirits, and by extension the drinks themselves.

clue.text: Brief comment from person apprehended by a copper

indicators.note: being apprehended means being held, so the abbreviation is held inside the others

parts.note: taken as written
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
per is the grammatical abbreviation for person

explanation.surface: A quip from a suspect arrested by a policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests a police officer but stands for the metal's chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperçu is a short, insightful remark or summary, a pithy observation.

clue.text: A lot of anger among most of selected singers

indicators.note: among means in the midst of, so one piece sits inside the other
a lot of means not quite all, so the final letter goes

parts.note: chose means selected

indicators.note: most of means nearly all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: ire is anger

explanation.surface: Plenty of fury breaking out among a hand-picked group of vocalists.
explanation.walkthrough: IRE loses its last letter to IR, and CHOSE loses its last to CHOS, which then holds IR.
explanation.definitionFit: Choirs are organised groups of singers, as in a church or concert.

clue.text: Running glory in race starts to please healthy character

parts.note: hie is an old word meaning hurry or race

indicators.note: running suggests letters set in motion and rearranged

parts.note: letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters

parts.note: first letters of please and healthy

explanation.surface: A runner's glory in the race, with a nod to keeping healthy.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface puts glory inside race, but the pieces simply follow one another. Hie is an archaic verb for hurry, kept alive by crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A hieroglyph is a pictorial character in Egyptian writing, a written symbol.

clue.text: Spot threat to crops — time to get away

indicators.note: getting away means departing, so that letter leaves the word

parts.note: swarms of locusts devastate crops
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Seeing a menace to the harvest and urging it to leave in time.
explanation.definitionFit: Locus is Latin for place, used in English for a particular location or position.

clue.text: Feature of space station bearing feature of door?

parts.note: air means bearing or manner, as in an air of confidence
a lock is something fitted to a door

explanation.surface: A puzzle asking what part of a space station also bears on a door.
explanation.definitionFit: An airlock is the sealed chamber that lets astronauts pass between a pressurised station and open space.

clue.text: Lamenting perverse political stance

indicators.note: perverse means twisted or contrary, so the letters are twisted out of order

parts.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone bemoaning a wrong-headed party line.
explanation.definitionFit: A party's or country's alignment is where it stands, the side it aligns itself with.

clue.text: Ramble a bit — article in memory or nothing in memory?

indicators.note: in places one piece within another

parts.note: ROM is read-only memory in a computer
a is the indefinite article
an alternative route to the same letters: O (nothing) inside RAM, random-access memory

explanation.surface: A question whether to wander back over a memory or let it go.
explanation.walkthrough: There are two routes: A inside ROM, or O (nothing) inside RAM, random-access memory; both give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To roam is to wander or ramble about without fixed purpose.

clue.text: Give later instructions about deliveries on journey

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries
a ride is a journey

explanation.surface: A dispatcher issuing new orders about parcels already on their way.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the bowler's balls are deliveries, six to an over.
explanation.definitionFit: To override is to cancel earlier orders by issuing new ones that take precedence.

clue.text: Important management group is a source of notes?

parts.note: key means important
a board of directors manages a company

explanation.surface: The company's board being where the memos come from.
explanation.walkthrough: Notes suggests memos from management, but the musical sense is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing the keys of a piano or synthesiser keyboard produces musical tones.

clue.text: Wear down recent royal elegy?

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, was the recent Queen
an elegy is a kind of lyric poem, as is an ode

explanation.surface: Mourning verse for a late monarch that is worn thin by repetition.
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth II, who died in 2022, hence recent.
explanation.definitionFit: To erode is to wear away gradually, as water and weather do to rock.

clue.text: Hesitation entering a US city after smart tricks

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the hesitation sound is placed within the city's letters

parts.note: chic means smart and stylish
taken as written
NY is New York
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A pause on arrival in an American city after some slick trickery.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as hesitation inside a US city coming after smart; the definition sits at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicanery is deception or trickery, especially in legal or political dealings.

clue.text: Wrong engaging in vehicular sex in green belt?

definitions.note: whimsical: a band of forest absorbing carbon

indicators.note: engaging in means getting involved within, so the misdeed goes inside the next phrase

parts.note: a bonk (British slang for sex) in a car
a sin is a wrong

explanation.surface: A tabloid tale of sinful backseat sex in a lay-by in the countryside around a town.
explanation.walkthrough: A green belt is normally protected land round a city; here it is any green zone soaking up carbon. Bonk is British slang for sex.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbon sink is a forest, soil or ocean that absorbs more carbon dioxide than it releases, a band of greenery working for the climate.

clue.text: Good spirits from writer having change of heart

indicators.note: a change of heart turns the central letters around while the ends stay put

parts.note: a Biro is a ballpoint pen, a writer

explanation.surface: An author cheering up after a change of mind.
explanation.walkthrough: Biro is the British brand name for a ballpoint pen; swapping its two middle letters gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Brio means vigour and liveliness, a lively high-spirited manner.

clue.text: Study exposed with English blokes in bondage to achieve climax

indicators.note: in bondage means held captive, so these pieces are held inside the other word

parts.note: a den is a study, a private room
out means exposed or revealed
E is the abbreviation for English
blokes, British slang, are men

explanation.surface: A racy scene of exposure and English men tied up, reaching a climax.
explanation.walkthrough: The bondage and climax are pure innuendo; the definition is the final unravelling of a plot.
explanation.definitionFit: A dénouement is the climax or resolution of a story, where the strands of the plot are drawn together.

clue.text: Historic Impressionist version of exile in Italy?

parts.note: historic means old
an impressionist pretends to be someone else

explanation.surface: An art-historical note about an exiled French painter's version of an Italian scene.
explanation.walkthrough: Impressionist suggests Monet or Renoir but means a mimic. The Old Pretender, James Francis Edward Stuart, claimant to the British throne, lived his exile in Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jacobite claimant James Stuart spent decades in papal Rome, so he was literally an exile living in Italy.

clue.text: Musical piece in examination? Stick around

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the first word wraps the second

parts.note: to paste is to stick
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A music student sitting an exam and told to stick around.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits before the question mark, with the container's parts in the second half.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastorale is a composition evoking rural life, as in Beethoven's Pastoral Symphony.

clue.text: Musical piece to repeat in revised version

indicators.note: a revised version is rewritten, so the letters are rewritten in a new order

parts.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A show tune due to be performed again in a reworked edition.
explanation.definitionFit: An operetta is a light opera with spoken dialogue, a short musical stage work.

clue.text: Investigation after error where books are kept

indicators.note: after places the investigation second, behind the error, reversing the clue's order

parts.note: a slip is a small error
a case is a police investigation

explanation.surface: An inquiry following a blunder in the place where the accounts are kept.
explanation.walkthrough: Books suggests financial records, but here they are real volumes.
explanation.definitionFit: A slipcase is a protective box, open at one end, for holding a book or set of books.

clue.text: First concern of slalom contestant?

definitions.note: adjective standing for a noun phrase meaning first place
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the leading place on a racing grid
second meaning, whimsical: a slalom skier must mind where the poles are placed

explanation.walkthrough: A slalom course is marked by poles the skier weaves between, so their placing really is the skier's worry.
explanation.definitionFit: In motor racing, the front spot on the starting grid, earned by the fastest qualifier, is the lead place.

clue.text: Appropriate to turn up before end of French colonial meal

indicators.note: turning up in a down entry means reading upward, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: fit means appropriate
fin is French for end

explanation.surface: A suitable way to round off a French colonial dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: End of French looks like a final letter but means the French word for end.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiffin was the light lunch of British India, a meal of the colonial era.

clue.text: Breach area in climbing in pursuit of that woman

parts.note: her refers to that woman

indicators.note: climbing in a down entry means going upward, so these letters read backwards

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area
taken as written

explanation.surface: A climber chasing a woman up a mountain and opening a breach.
explanation.walkthrough: Climbing works only in a down entry, where reading upward turns the letters around.
explanation.definitionFit: A hernia is a rupture, an organ breaking through the wall that should contain it.

clue.text: Fresh energy after indication of demise?

definitions.note: in the sense of cheeky or coarse, as in a ripe remark

indicators.note: after places the energy second, behind the sign of death, reversing the clue's order

parts.note: RIP, rest in peace, marks a death on a gravestone
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A burst of new vigour coming right after a sign of death.
explanation.walkthrough: Fresh looks like the opposite of ripe, but both can describe language that is cheeky or near the knuckle.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripe language is coarse or risqué, and a fresh remark is impudent, so the two adjectives overlap in that sense.

clue.text: Finally blue-pencil i.e. b_____, d__ and worse, possibly

definitions.text: Finally blue-pencil i.e. b_____, d__ and worse, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could be arranged some other way
finally points to the closing letter of the hyphenated word that follows

parts.note: the final letter of blue-pencil
taken as written
the lone letter shown
the lone letter shown
taken as written

explanation.surface: A censor's brief: cut words like bloody, damn and worse with a blue pencil.
explanation.walkthrough: The blanked-out b_____ and d__ are swear words with only their initials left, exactly what a censor does; to blue-pencil is to cut text.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Bowdler published an expurgated Shakespeare, so his name became the verb for censoring rude words from a text.

clue.text: Line taken in skilful porcelain

indicators.note: taken in means absorbed inside, so the letter goes within the other word

parts.note: deft means skilful
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A craftsman's skilful line painted on china.
explanation.definitionFit: Delft is the tin-glazed blue and white pottery named after the Dutch town where it was made.

clue.text: Unaccompanied, but very much upset in this city

indicators.note: upset in a down entry means turned over, and very much names the part of the word that flips

parts.note: solo means unaccompanied

explanation.surface: A lone traveller very upset in a foreign city.
explanation.walkthrough: So means very much, as in so tired; only those first two letters of the word are flipped, the rest stays put.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital city of Norway, its largest urban centre.

clue.text: Studies, having ignored one bog, requiring return around a part of South Africa

indicators.note: ignoring one means leaving out the letter that looks like the numeral one

parts.note: trains as a verb means studies or practises

indicators.note: return means turning back, so the word for a toilet is read right to left
around means surrounding, so the reversed word encloses the article

parts.note: bog and lav are both British slang for a toilet
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone skipping a toilet stop on a long return journey through South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Bog suggests a marsh but is British slang for a toilet, and studies is a verb here, as in practises.
explanation.definitionFit: The Transvaal was a province of South Africa north of the Vaal river, now split among several modern provinces.

clue.text: Small force blocking river in retreat

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the river's name runs right to left
blocking means standing in the way, so the letter sits inside the river

parts.note: the Nile, Africa's great river
F is the symbol for force in physics

explanation.surface: A modest army barring the way along a river as it falls back.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin describes something small and delicate, like an elf.

clue.text: Wonderful start to analysis — our team then associated with mass and energy

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: first letter of analysis
a team speaking of itself says we
so means then, as in so we left
M is the symbol for mass
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A physics team marvelling at its first analysis linking mass and energy, as Einstein did.
explanation.walkthrough: Mass and energy evoke E = mc squared, but each simply stands for its one-letter symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Awesome in its casual sense means excellent or wonderful.

clue.text: Shakespearean heroine, one failing to complete sea voyage, mostly — Miranda, ultimately?

indicators.note: mostly means not all, so the final letter of the ship's name is dropped

parts.words: one failing to complete sea voyage
parts.note: the liner that sank on its maiden voyage in 1912

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the closing letter is kept

parts.note: last letter of Miranda

explanation.surface: Asks whether Miranda, the heroine of The Tempest's sea voyage, is ultimately the one.
explanation.walkthrough: Miranda is another Shakespeare heroine, and The Tempest opens with a shipwreck, a neat decoy for the actual queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Titania is the queen of the fairies in A Midsummer Night's Dream, one of Shakespeare's leading female roles.
